{{Short description|Theorem in analytic number theory}}
In [[number theory]], the '''fundamental lemma of sieve theory''' is any of several results that systematize the process of applying [[Sieve theory|sieve methods]] to particular problems. [[Heini Halberstam|Halberstam]] & [[Hans-Egon Richert|Richert]]
<ref name="HR">
{{cite book | last = Halberstam | first = Heini |author-link=Heini Halberstam | first2=Hans-Egon | last2=Richert |authorlink2=Hans-Egon Richert | title = Sieve Methods | publisher = Academic Press | location = London | year = 1974 | isbn = 0-12-318250-6 | mr = 0424730 | series=London Mathematical Society Monographs | volume=4}}
</ref>{{Rp|92–93}}
write:
{{quote|A curious feature of sieve literature is that while there is frequent use of [[Brun sieve|Brun's ''method'']] there are only a few attempts to formulate a general Brun ''theorem'' (such as Theorem 2.1); as a result there are surprisingly many papers which repeat in considerable detail the steps of Brun's argument.}}
Diamond & [[Heini Halberstam|Halberstam]]<ref name="DH">
{{cite book | last1= Diamond | first1 = Harold G. | last2 = Halberstam | first2 = Heini | authorlink2 = Heini Halberstam | others = With William F. Galway | title = A Higher-Dimensional Sieve Method: with Procedures for Computing Sieve Functions |series= Cambridge Tracts in Mathematics |volume=177 | publisher = Cambridge University Press | location = Cambridge | year = 2008 | isbn = 978-0-521-89487-6 }}</ref>{{Rp|42}}
attribute the terminology ''Fundamental Lemma'' to [[Jonas Kubilius]].

==Common notation==
We use these notations:
* <math>A</math> is a set of <math>X</math> positive integers, and <math>A_d</math> is its subset of integers divisible by <math>d</math>
* <math>w(d)</math> and <math>R_d</math> are functions of <math>A</math> and of <math>d</math> that estimate the number of elements of <math>A</math> that are divisible by <math>d</math>, according to the formula
:<math> \left\vert A_d \right\vert = \frac{w(d)}{d} X + R_d . </math>
:Thus <math>w(d)/d</math> represents an approximate density of members divisible by ''<math>d</math>'', and <math>R_d</math> represents an error or remainder term.
* <math>P</math> is a set of primes, and <math>P(z)</math> is the product of those primes <math>\leq z</math>
* <math>S(A, P, z)</math> is the number of elements of <math>A</math> not divisible by any prime in <math>P</math> that is <math>\leq z</math>
* <math>\kappa</math> is a constant, called the sifting density,<ref name="Greaves" />{{Rp|28}} that appears in the assumptions below. It is a [[weighted average]] of the number of [[residue class]]es sieved out by each prime.

==Fundamental lemma of the combinatorial sieve==
This formulation is from Tenenbaum.<ref name="Tenenbaum">
{{cite book | last = Tenenbaum | first = Gérald | title = Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory | publisher = Cambridge University Press | location = Cambridge | year = 1995 | isbn = 0-521-41261-7 }}
</ref>{{Rp|60}} Other formulations are in [[Heini Halberstam|Halberstam]] & [[Hans-Egon Richert|Richert]],<ref name="HR" />{{Rp|82}} in Greaves,<ref name="Greaves">
{{cite book | last = Greaves | first = George | title = Sieves in Number Theory | publisher = Springer | location = Berlin | year = 2001 | isbn = 3-540-41647-1 }}
</ref>{{Rp|92}}
and in [[John Friedlander|Friedlander]] & [[Henryk Iwaniec|Iwaniec]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Friedlander |first=John |author-link=John Friedlander |author2=Henryk Iwaniec |author2-link=Henryk Iwaniec |year=1978 |title=On Bombieri's asymptotic sieve |journal=Annali della Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa; Classe di Scienze |series=4e série |volume=5 |issue=4 |pages=719–756 |url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=ASNSP_1978_4_5_4_719_0 |accessdate=2009-02-14 }}</ref>{{Rp|732–733}}
We make the assumptions:
* <math>w(d)</math> is a [[multiplicative function]].
* The sifting density <math>\kappa</math> satisfies, for some constant <math>C</math> and any real numbers <math>\eta</math> and <math>\xi</math> with <math>2\leq \eta\leq \xi</math>:
:<math>\prod_{\eta \le p \le \xi} \left( 1 - \frac{w(p)}{p} \right) ^{-1} < \left( \frac{\ln \xi}{\ln \eta} \right) ^\kappa \left( 1 + \frac{C}{\ln \eta} \right). </math>

There is a parameter <math>u\geq 1</math> that is at our disposal. We have uniformly in <math>A</math>, ''<math>X</math>'', ''<math>z</math>'', and <math>u</math> that
:<math>S(a,P,z) = X \prod_{p \le z, p \in P} \left( 1 - \frac{w(p)}{p} \right) \{1 + O(u^{-u/2})\} + O\left(\sum_{d \le z^u, d|P(z)} |R_d| \right).</math>
In applications we pick ''<math>u</math>'' to get the best error term. In the sieve it is related to the number of levels of the [[inclusion–exclusion principle]].

==Fundamental lemma of the Selberg sieve==
This formulation is from [[Heini Halberstam|Halberstam]] & [[Hans-Egon Richert|Richert]].<ref name="HR" />{{Rp|208–209}} Another formulation is in Diamond & [[Heini Halberstam|Halberstam]].<ref name="DH" />{{Rp|29}}

We make the assumptions:
* <math>w(d)</math> is a [[multiplicative function]].
* The sifting density <math>\kappa</math> satisfies, for some constant <math>C</math> and any real numbers <math>\eta</math> and <math>\xi</math> with <math>2\leq \eta\leq \xi</math>: 
<math> \qquad \sum_{\eta \le p \le \xi} \frac{w(p) \ln p}{p} < \kappa  \ln \frac{\xi}{\eta} + C. </math>
* ''<math>\frac{w(p)}{p} < 1-c</math>'' for some small fixed ''<math>c</math>'' and all ''<math>p</math>''.
* ''<math>|R(d)|\leq w(d)</math>'' for all squarefree ''<math>d</math>'' whose prime factors are in ''<math>P</math>''.

The fundamental lemma has almost the same form as for the combinatorial sieve. Write ''<math>u = \ln{X} /\ln{z}</math>''. The conclusion is:

:<math>S(a,P,z) = X \prod_{p \le z,\ p \in P} \left( 1 - \frac{w(p)}{p} \right) \{1 + O(e^{-u/2})\}.</math>

Note that ''<math>u</math>'' is no longer an independent parameter at our disposal, but is controlled by the choice of ''<math>z</math>''.

Note that the error term here is weaker than for the fundamental lemma of the combinatorial sieve. Halberstam & Richert remark:<ref name="HR" />{{Rp|221}} "Thus it is not true to say, as has been asserted from time to time in the literature, that Selberg's sieve is always better than Brun's."
